topic: Sharp single-bin facet envelope for arbitrary finite coarsened-exposure IV bounds. Observe iid (Z,X,Y) with randomized binary Z, binary Y, finite X={a,b,c_1,...,c_m}, and a declared trusted set T containing a,b whose category interventions are well defined and satisfy exclusion and consistency; untrusted categories impose no cross-Z outcome restriction. For theta_ab=E[Y(b)-Y(a)], prove the identified interval is sharp and its lower/upper endpoints are the eight binary-exposure Balke-Pearl affine pieces plus exactly two pieces per trusted nuisance category. Derive a complete two-diagonal transport reduction, explicit endpoint-attaining finite response laws, the exact strict-improvement criterion for adding trust, and invariance to splitting or merging wholly untrusted bins. Give an O(|X|) endpoint/active-face evaluator and finite-sample simultaneous whole-set inference valid at ties and zero cells. Consumer: Du Toit et al.'s LEAP adherence analysis, where the theorem determines whether separately justified intermediate exposure categories can change the assumption-free low-versus-high consumption interval. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Coupling the two instrument-arm factual responses on a complete bipartite graph minus a partial matching reduces the lower endpoint to maximizing mass on two target diagonals. After reserving those masses, feasibility has two individual caps and one total cap per trusted nuisance outcome cell; exact maximization yields the claimed affine envelope, and a finite augmenting-path completion constructs attaining laws. Checks passed 840 response-LP cases for 2-8 exposure categories and all trust cardinalities, 32 saturated-response cases, and 9,648 exact rational endpoint constructions; maximum LP discrepancy was 7.78e-16. LEAP arm denominators 305 and 312 reproduce the low-minus-high interval [-5073/31720,10/61]. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently formalize and verify the transport domination and endpoint-completion argument; the optional moment-selected Gaussian multiplier procedure still needs a uniform local-tie/vanishing-variance proof, while finite-sample Hoeffding whole-set coverage is already derived. EARLY KILL TEST: Enumerate legal denominator-three four-category tables under every trust subset containing a,b and reconstruct both reserved-diagonal endpoint laws exactly; stop if any residual flow, margin, or objective equality fails. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_coarsened_iv_facet_envelope.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp pairwise ATE interval for a binary outcome and binary randomized instrument when treatment has arbitrarily many categories but exclusion and consistency are asserted only for a designated subset containing the two target categories.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves the coarsened-exposure pattern only for two or three well-defining levels and identifies extension to arbitrary exposure levels as ongoing research.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Arvid Sjölander

source_refs.claim: The arbitrary-finite categorical-IV characterization imposes exclusion across every treatment category rather than a category-specific trusted subset.
source_refs.author: Yilin Song, F. Richard Guo, K. C. Gary Chan, and Thomas S. Richardson

source_refs.claim: For binary instrument, treatment, and outcome, the sharp ATE interval is the envelope of eight affine response-type LP pieces.
source_refs.author: Alexander Balke and Judea Pearl
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Gabriel et al. provide the ternary mixed-validity boundary and explicitly leave arbitrary exposure cardinality open, while Song et al. occupy the arbitrary-cardinality full-validity case. Neither source gives a closed-form projection when only selected nuisance categories possess well-defined, exclusion-respecting potential outcomes. Category-specific exclusion removes only a partial matching from the arm-to-response compatibility graph, so Song et al.'s global Strassen relation and the ordinary Balke–Pearl reduction do not directly prove a linear-size facet envelope or furnish endpoint-attaining joint response laws.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient identified interval whose endpoints consist of the eight Balke–Pearl affine faces plus exactly two faces per trusted nuisance category, together with finite response laws attaining both endpoints for every finite category count.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames why some coarsened exposure levels define credible interventions while others cannot support exclusion, then connects that distinction to partial identification and LEAP.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Realized adherence is fine-grained but scientific interventions are coarsened -> only some levels define credible interventions -> existing mixed-validity results stop at small supports -> arbitrary finite mixed-validity sharp bounds are needed.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode finite response functions as a linear program, obtain symbolic faces from dual extreme points, and prove tightness using primal response distributions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired interval is a projection of a finite response-function polytope, but its claimed linear number of faces requires exploiting structure beyond generic enumeration.

method_exemplars.technique: Use finite-set Strassen compatibility on a bipartite coherence graph and prove necessity, sufficiency, and nonredundancy of the induced inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its transport compatibility proof is closest to completing armwise factual margins with a common counterfactual law; the first changed step is replacing global coherence with a partial-matching-deletion relation.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed a multinomial KL confidence region for observed arm distributions into the sharp-bound convex program to obtain simultaneous finite-sample coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly supplies inference for linear causal functionals in finite categorical-IV models and remains valid at sparse or zero cells.

open_problems.open_problem: Give an exact observable criterion for when declaring one additional nuisance exposure category well defined and exclusion-respecting strictly narrows either endpoint of a pairwise coarsened-exposure IV interval.

source_refs.claim: A well-defining third level contributes additional endpoint terms, yet in the LEAP example trusting the intermediate level does not change the numerical interval.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Arvid Sjölander

source_refs.claim: Using all valid categorical treatment levels gives bounds no wider, and sometimes strictly tighter, than binary reductions, without characterizing strictness for one newly trusted category.
source_refs.author: Yilin Song, F. Richard Guo, K. C. Gary Chan, and Thomas S. Richardson

source_refs.claim: LEAP randomized infants to sustained peanut consumption or avoidance, while realized consumption varied enough to motivate low, intermediate, and high adherence categories.
source_refs.author: George Du Toit et al.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature establishes only weak monotonicity of information: extra valid categories cannot widen a sharp set. It supplies examples of both strict tightening and no change, including LEAP's intermediate bin, but no data-level condition identifying exactly when a new nuisance-category face overtakes the existing envelope. Investigators therefore cannot determine from observed arm-cell probabilities whether the scientific effort required to justify an intermediate-category intervention has identification value.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient system of strict affine inequalities in observed arm-cell probabilities characterizing improvement of the lower endpoint, upper endpoint, and total interval width after adding a specified category to the trusted set.

writing_exemplar.why: Its LEAP analysis poses the practical decision of whether separately defending the intermediate adherence intervention changes the low-versus-high conclusion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Intermediate adherence is observed and potentially intervention-relevant -> validating it imposes additional cross-arm restrictions -> those restrictions may or may not tighten the target interval -> an exact value-of-trust criterion determines when validation matters.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent each endpoint as an envelope of finitely many LP-dual affine functionals and compare the active dual faces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Strict improvement is an active-face replacement question relative to the eight baseline Balke–Pearl pieces.

method_exemplars.technique: Use one finite-sample confidence region for all multinomial cells before projecting several causal functionals simultaneously.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sampling variation can change the active face, so inference on strict improvement requires joint control of all cell probabilities and competing faces.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when splitting or merging nuisance exposure bins leaves the sharp pairwise IV bounds unchanged under category-specific well-definedness and exclusion assumptions.

source_refs.claim: In the homocysteine example, changing from three exposure bins to four produced the same numerical bounds, but no general refinement-invariance theorem is given.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Arvid Sjölander

source_refs.claim: Coarsening treatment intensity can distort conventional IV estimands by inducing an exclusion failure, so invariance requires a carefully stated trust boundary.
source_refs.author: John Marshall

source_refs.claim: A many-to-one coarsening of treatment versions generally changes intervention interpretation unless suitable version-equivalence or policy conditions hold.
source_refs.author: Tyler J. VanderWeele and Miguel A. Hernán

open_problems.why_unsolved: The empirical equality reported by Gabriel et al. may reflect a structural aggregation property rather than coincidence. Marshall and VanderWeele–Hernán show why unrestricted coarsening is generally consequential: it can conceal outcome-relevant versions, invalidate exclusion, or change the estimand. The missing boundary theorem must distinguish refinements wholly inside the unrestricted nuisance region from refinements that create, destroy, or merge a trusted intervention level; generic categorical-IV polytope descriptions do not expose this quotient structure.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if aggregation theorem showing that the identified interval factors through armwise totals over wholly untrusted bins, paired with a finite counterexample showing failure when a merge crosses a trusted-category boundary.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates coarsening through dose and adherence data and reports the three-bin/four-bin equality that a general theorem would explain.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fine-grained adherence is routinely binned -> analysts can choose different nuisance-bin resolutions -> an application exhibits unchanged bounds after refinement -> characterize which refinements are identification-neutral.

method_exemplars.technique: Express compatibility through a finite bipartite relation and compare projected polytopes under maps that aggregate observed categories.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Refinement invariance asserts that two compatibility polytopes have the same projection onto the pairwise ATE, naturally inviting transport pushforward and lifting arguments.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate treatment labels from underlying versions and state consistency at the intervention level before deriving identification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the conceptual distinction required to explain why aggregation within an untrusted region can be harmless while aggregation of well-defined versions need not be.

method_exemplars.technique: Project a simultaneous multinomial confidence region through the categorical-IV feasible set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same construction can support simultaneous comparison of bounds computed under several candidate binning schemes.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop a less-conservative simultaneous Gaussian-multiplier procedure for coarsened-exposure IV bound endpoints that remains uniformly valid under local affine-face ties, zero-probability cells, and vanishing face variances.

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies conservative simultaneous finite-sample KL-region inference for categorical-IV bounds and leaves less-conservative confidence intervals for future work.
source_refs.author: Yilin Song, F. Richard Guo, K. C. Gary Chan, and Thomas S. Richardson

source_refs.claim: The coarsened-exposure applications use parametric or m-out-of-n bootstrap intervals rather than a uniform active-face result for arbitrary finite envelopes.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Arvid Sjölander

source_refs.claim: For max/min-type directionally differentiable functionals, the ordinary bootstrap generally fails and inference must account for the directional derivative.
source_refs.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos

source_refs.claim: Intersection-bound inference uses Gaussian approximation and adaptive inequality selection to handle suprema and infima of estimated bounding functions.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Sokbae Lee, and Adam M. Rosen

open_problems.why_unsolved: An explicit affine envelope makes point estimation inexpensive but becomes nonregular when several pieces tie. Ordinary bootstrap inconsistency follows from directional rather than full differentiability, while studentized moment selection becomes discontinuous when a cell or contrast variance approaches zero. Song et al.'s KL construction covers these boundary cases but is deliberately conservative; the missing proof is uniform local validity of multiplier critical values and an estimated near-active set across simultaneous tie and degeneracy sequences.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A simultaneous confidence set for both sharp endpoints with a uniform coverage theorem over multinomial triangular arrays allowing local face ties and vanishing variances, an explicit multiplier critical-value algorithm, and a first-order width improvement over finite-sample concentration inference away from degeneracy.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates categorical-IV identification from finite-sample uncertainty and directly motivates reducing conservatism.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Categorical-IV restrictions yield a sharp set -> plug-in endpoints are nonsmooth projections -> concentration regions guarantee coverage but are conservative -> sharper inference is needed without sacrificing validity at nonregular configurations.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Gaussian strong approximation to an envelope of estimated bounding functions and use adaptive inequality selection to retain near-binding faces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each endpoint is a finite intersection bound whose active affine pieces correspond to near-binding inequalities.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate and bootstrap the directional derivative of a nondifferentiable max/min map rather than bootstrapping the original functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At face ties, the endpoint map has the same max/min directional derivative; the new work must extend validity to vanishing covariance directions.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct multinomial confidence regions using a uniform Chernoff-type tail bound for empirical relative entropy.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This provides a boundary-safe fallback and benchmark for demonstrating precision gains without losing zero-cell coverage.

open_problems.open_problem: Replace binary all-or-nothing trust in nuisance exposure categories with category-specific bounds on exclusion violations and derive the resulting sharp sensitivity path for the low-versus-high pairwise ATE.

source_refs.claim: The paper contrasts well-defining nuisance levels with fully contaminated or ill-defining levels but does not interpolate between those regimes.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Arvid Sjölander

source_refs.claim: The paper relaxes exclusion by bounding or modeling a direct instrument effect, but does so in a linear IV model rather than a finite-response coarsened-exposure model.
source_refs.author: Timothy G. Conley, Christian B. Hansen, and Peter E. Rossi

source_refs.claim: Automated polynomial programming can numerically relax discrete causal assumptions with sharpness guarantees but does not give a closed-form category-specific sensitivity envelope.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, and Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: The trusted-set model jumps from exact exclusion to unrestricted direct effects for each nuisance category. Conley et al. demonstrate the value of graded exclusion sensitivity, but their linear direct-effect parameter does not translate into sharp constraints on binary potential-response cells. Category-specific caps soften the transport compatibility relation rather than merely deleting edges, so the hard partial-matching domination step must be replaced. Generic automated bounds can certify instances but do not expose analytical breakpoints or constructive attainability.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Sharp piecewise-affine lower and upper bounds as functions of category-specific exclusion-violation radii, including every breakpoint, endpoint-attaining finite response laws, and reductions to the trusted and unrestricted envelopes at the limiting radii.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing treats exclusion as scientifically plausible but rarely exact, which transfers naturally to graded confidence in intermediate adherence categories.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact exclusion is substantively contestable -> abandoning an instrument wastes information -> bound the magnitude of violation -> report a sensitivity path for the causal conclusion.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode relaxed causal restrictions as polynomial constraints and use certified dual relaxations with spatial branch-and-bound to obtain sharp numerical benchmarks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It can validate candidate symbolic sensitivity faces and endpoint constructions under bounded category-specific violations.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive symbolic sharp bounds from response-function primal and dual programs when relaxed restrictions remain linear.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If the category-specific direct-effect caps admit a linear response-type encoding, its dual-face method is the closest route to the requested piecewise-affine sensitivity envelope.

method_exemplars.technique: Project a simultaneous finite-sample multinomial confidence region through a categorical-IV convex program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same projection strategy can give whole-path or selected-radius coverage after the cap-indexed sharp region is characterized.

literature_map:
1. Balke and Pearl (1997, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.1997.10474074) provide the foundational eight-piece sharp binary-IV ATE envelope via response-function linear programming.
2. Gabriel, Sachs, and Sjölander (2025, Biostatistics, arXiv:2401.17735) distinguish well- from ill-defining coarsened exposure levels and explicitly leave extension of their small-support pattern to arbitrary exposure cardinality open.
3. Gabriel et al. show that a trusted third level can add sharp faces, whereas a fully contaminated nuisance level collapses to the binary Balke–Pearl information.
4. Their LEAP reanalysis finds the same low-versus-high interval whether the intermediate-consumption category is trusted or unrestricted.
5. Their homocysteine example also gives the same bounds under three-bin and four-bin codings, motivating a structural refinement-invariance question.
6. Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson (arXiv:2405.09510v6, 2026) sharply characterize the fully valid categorical-IV model for arbitrary finite supports using finite-set Strassen theory.
7. Song et al. occupy the full-trust arbitrary-category case but do not permit exclusion to hold only on a selected subset of treatment categories.
8. Song et al. give conservative simultaneous finite-sample KL-region inference and identify less-conservative confidence intervals as future work.
9. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjölander, and Gabriel (2023, JCGS, arXiv:2003.10702) provide symbolic LP-duality machinery, while Duarte et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2109.13471) provide certified numerical sharp-bound benchmarks.
10. VanderWeele and Hernán (2013, Journal of Causal Inference, DOI 10.1515/jci-2012-0002) show that coarsened labels conceal treatment versions and require intervention-level consistency reasoning.
11. Marshall (2016, Political Analysis, DOI 10.1093/pan/mpw007) shows that treatment coarsening can distort IV estimands, so invariance must be confined to a carefully defined nuisance region.
12. Du Toit et al. (2015, NEJM, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1414850) provide the LEAP adherence setting in which validation of an intermediate category has direct consumer value.
13. Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013, Econometrica, arXiv:0907.3503) and Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud, arXiv:1404.3763) provide active-face and directional-differentiability machinery for tie-robust endpoint inference.
14. Guo and Richardson (2021, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, arXiv:2003.08614) supply zero-cell-safe multinomial KL concentration, while Conley, Hansen, and Rossi (2012, ReStat) motivate graded rather than binary exclusion sensitivity.
